Committing fresh cash before that resyncs risks double-spending money that's already gone into positions you don't know you have. Resync via IBKR first — that's the actual highest-value action available today, not a new trade idea.

🔄 Rotation: N/A — no open positions to rotate out of.

📚 Today you learned

Order Duration Types — Day, GTC, IOC, FOK

Every order carries a duration, not just a price. A Day order dies at the close if unfilled — cleanest for anything you don't want haunting your book. GTC (good-til-canceled) sits on the book for weeks or months until filled or manually pulled — which is exactly the trap you're in right now: your AXTI and GOOG buy limits from Aug 4 are GTC, meaning they've been silently live this entire time regardless of whether you were watching. IOC (immediate-or-cancel) fills whatever it can right now and kills the rest — useful for large size where you don't want a resting order to leak your intent. FOK (fill-or-kill) is all-or-nothing, instantly. Forex mostly trades Day-equivalent by convention; equities give you the choice, and GTC's convenience is exactly why it needs a standing reminder to check it, not a "set and forget."

Also today: Working order — the exchange-side term for any order still resting unfilled, which is what your IBKR order-status screen would call AXTI and GOOG right now if either is still genuinely open.
